notes: Identity assessment: title Does inhibition cause forgetting after selective retrieval? A reanalysis and failure to replicate; Kevin W. Potter, Lucas D. Huszar and David E. Huber; DOI 10.1016/j.cortex.2018.03.026; Cortex 104 (2018), 26–45. The supplied text contains the primary Research report with methods, results, discussion and references, rather than an abstract-only parse. No PDF path was supplied, so no rendering was possible. The source is the primary Potter, Huszar & Huber (2018) report, but the target sample cannot be identified uniquely. The locator p.25 matches neither a supplied-text page (20 article pages) nor a printed article page (26–45). The neutral neural-pattern description does not distinguish the behavioral replications or identify a critical test. The label study 2 alone does not establish whether it refers to the authors’ second replication attempt or to the second main-text replication (the third, preregistered attempt). Candidate analytic participant counts are explicitly 22 for the second attempt and 48 for the third/preregistered attempt; the latter also has low-intrusion and high-visualization subgroups of 24 and 21. No count is assigned by numeric label or order. Candidate exclusions: second attempt reports 35 recruited, ten incorrect-instruction participants excluded, and 22 meeting inclusion criteria after chance-level practice/time-out screening; time-out responses removed. Its recruitment narrative also mentions an additional 11 after 25, inconsistent with the stated 35 total; no arithmetic reconciliation is imposed. Third attempt: 53 recruited, four did not complete and one supplied no selective-retrieval responses; explicitly 48 complete datasets, with no further subject exclusion or data trimming based on the earlier criteria. The subgroup counts overlap and must not be summed. No N was derived from degrees of freedom.
